market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.fact: NSPM's September poll had Student List at 44.4% and Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia at 41.7%. NSPM's previous poll had them at 39.6% and 37.5%. Four other lists were reported above the 3% threshold.

Faktor plus poll (Sept 16–20, n=986, about 62% expected turnout): United Serbia (SNS) 48.6%, Student List 37.1%, SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8%, Mi snaga naroda 1.2%. 16% of respondents were undecided.
Faktor plus's earlier poll had SNS at 47.2% and Student List at 31.5%. In the next poll the Student List rose 5.6 points and SNS 1.4 points.

recent_facts.source: CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab via Danas
recent_facts.fact: CRTA poll (June 10–24, face-to-face, n=2,324): among decided voters (about 70%), Student List 44.9%, SNS 35.7%, SPS 3.8%, and all others below the threshold. Wikipedia describes it as the first regular national poll since July 2010 with any option other than SNS in first place.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list PR in one nationwide constituency using D'Hondt, with a 3% threshold that is waived for ethnic minority lists. 126 seats are needed for a majority. Sixteen lists were registered, including United Serbia (SNS-led, headed by Vučić), SPS, European Serbia, Authentic Right (NADA) and the Student List (ballot holder Ilija Srdanović).

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as president on September 27, more than seven months before his term ended, after calling the snap election. Al Jazeera reported that polls suggest the race between his party and the student-backed list could be tight.
Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister at Belgrade's largest indoor arena, which thousands of supporters filled, and promised a 'comprehensive' victory.
Vučić dissolved the National Assembly on September 9 and called early elections for October 25, 2026, although the regular mandate ran to December 2027.

Students marched to register the 'Student List – Students Are Winning', a slate of 250 candidates. It is backed by many opposition parties, including DS, ZLF, Kreni-Promeni, SDS, LSV, Dveri and Enough is Enough. Some opposition parties are running separately, for example European Serbia (SSP and others).

In the March 29, 2026 local elections in 10 municipalities, SNS and its partners won all 10 and student-backed lists came second in each. The ruling coalition's share fell compared with the previous elections in 8 of the 10. Examples: Smederevska Palanka, SNS 58% vs. students 29.2%; Aranđelovac, students 46.08% (20 of 41 seats).
